extracted_by: hand, T-0292 — the Democrat read, October 1834; page 2's two gambling meetings added by hand, T-0997
note: Vol. I No. 48. The town is on page 2 AND page 3. Page 3 completes the fire ordinance begun on 1834-10-01 — the trustees met at the Tremont House on 13 October and gave the wardens command at a fire, in force from 25 October — and it carries no Chicago letter list, only the Hennepin and Plainfield ones, which are recorded and not minted. PAGE 2 COLUMNS 1-2 ARE TWO TOWN MEETINGS AGAINST GAMBLING (T-0997), the second of which appointed a committee of seventy and is the largest single list of named townspeople in this corpus outside the post-office returns. Both are read through an interleaving the transcription does not resolve: the column-2 and column-3 crops are Tesseract fallbacks that straddle the gutter, so each of their lines carries the right edge of one printed column and then the left of the next. c006-c011 name the halves separately with `spans` and say per name which half a name came from; a narrow band of characters between two crops is in neither reading, and every name it swallowed is left `[?]` in the position it was printed rather than conjectured.

claims.notes: THE COMMITTEE OF SEVENTY, AND WHERE IT BEGINS. This is the foot of page 2 column 1, as the Vision reading of that column caught it — and that reading is the LEFT-HAND PART of each printed line only. The right-hand part of these same lines was caught by the Tesseract crop that follows, and is quoted at c007; the two must be read together and neither is the line. A narrow band of characters between the two crops is in neither, which is why a surname can stand here with its initial unread and no conjecture can supply it. The resolution itself is legible: a committee of seventy appointed, whose duty it shall be on all occasions to take notice of and report to the authorities every infraction of the laws against gambling. The list starts in these last five lines and runs on into column 2 (c008).

claims.notes: THE RIGHT-HAND PART OF THE LINES c006 QUOTES. The transcription's column-2 crop is a Tesseract fallback that straddles the gutter: every line of it carries the right edge of column 1 first and then column 2, so these spans name the column-1 half and the locator's column is the crop's own marker rather than the print's. The splice is not asserted, it is demonstrated: line 951's 'a commuttee of 70 he app' joins line 1090's 'einted' into one word, and line 963's 'Card, ine:' joins line 1100's 'ant Goodrich' into the Grant Goodrich the same page names again at c011. Line 1099 is not claimed because it carries no column-1 fragment at all. The names left unminted here are unminted because their surnames cannot be read, not because they were not printed: 'Hassleme' at c006 line 960, 'Mloed' at line 1101, 'H. Kee' at line 1097 and the 'Willia[m]' at line 1098 whose surname fell in the band between the two crops. GOODRICH IS READ AND NOT MINTED. The line joins to '[Gr]ant Goodrich' and the same page names Grant Goodrich again at c011, but the 'Gr' itself is in the band between two crops and no reading here contains it. A resident card is not the place to spend a letter nothing read, so the name stands in this claim's reading and mints nobody; the page images would settle it in a line.

claims.notes: THE OTHER MEETING ON THIS PAGE, AND ITS COMMITTEE. Column 1 carries two town meetings against gambling, not one: the first adjourns to Saturday the 25th (lines 992-995) and the second is datelined 'Oct. 25th, 1834' at line 998, so everything above 998 belongs to the earlier meeting. These seven spans are that meeting's committee, in the column-1 half of the crop — the same half c007 reads lower down the column. The Vision reading of column 1 supplies the other half of line 986 as 'Willen Forsyth, Grant' (transcription line 875), which is what makes 'Goodiich' Grant Goodrich rather than a guess. NOT MINTED: 'H. G. Hub[bard]' (983), because the '3' before it is an initial nothing can read and G. Hubbard and E. K. Hubbard are both available on this page; 'Hon. R. J' (988) and 'E. K' (989), whose surnames fell in the band between the crops; 'G. Springs' (990), a surname the line breaks off rather than finishes. This claim is filed because leaving it out would have left the page half-read and the next run re-deriving the same two-meeting structure from scratch. THE FORENAME AT LINE 984 IS EXPANDED AND SAID SO. The crop cuts the line's first letter, so what it holds is 'no. SC. Hogav.'; 'no.' is not a forename and 'Jno.' is the printer's ordinary contraction of John, which is how the town's own card for its postmaster already spells him. The normalized name is therefore John S. C. Hogan and the as-printed string keeps what the crop actually carries.
